*South32 Advancing Work on Peake Copper Deposit as Fast as It Can, CEO Says
South32's New CEO Says Under No Pressure to Replace Aluminum via M&A — Interview
By Rhiannon Hoyle
South32's new chief executive officer signaled he won't be racing out to make acquisitions to replace the aluminum business that the Australia-based miner is selling to Alcoa.

Yet, speaking in an interview, Matt Daley left the door open to exploring deals in time, as South32 reshapes its business around copper and zinc, two metals it views as critical to a transition to lower-carbon energy.

South32 in July said it will sell its aluminum assets to the U.S. company in a cash-and-stock deal that is valued at up to $5.6 billion and is expected to be completed in the first half of 2027. After the deal was disclosed, some analysts questioned whether the miner could be about to take a more aggressive approach to inorganic growth.

"By no means is there a requirement for us to rush out and replace aluminum with something else," said Daley. "We're very much attuned to just creating value for our shareholders. For us, that's very clear in the near term. Beyond that, we'll weigh up our options."

Daley was speaking after South32 on Thursday reported a fivefold increase in annual net profit and said it would do away with its fixed payout ratio for dividends as the company puts a bigger focus on growth.

Daley, who last month succeeded South32's CEO of more than 11 years, Graham Kerr, said his near-term priorities include closing the aluminum sale and extracting "maximum value" from South32's existing operations.
The miner already has an investment pipeline, including projects in the U.S., Australia and Chile, that can lift production volumes by about 55% over the next four or five years, he said.
"Obviously those growth options are really important to us," said Daley.
In the U.S., South32 is building a $3.3 billion zinc-lead-silver mine at a project called Hermosa in Arizona, where it expects to be in production by mid-2028.
Also at Hermosa, it is exploring the potential development of a copper deposit, called Peake, at a time when copper prices have been on a record-breaking rally due to concerns about supply shortages.
"We are moving Peake as fast as we can," said Daley.

The U.S. Forest Service in July released its final record of decision for Hermosa, completing a federal environmental review and approval process. South32 expects a subsequent so-called notice to proceed some time this quarter, a milestone that Daley said allows the miner to broaden its drilling activities to build its confidence in the size of the resource.

"At the moment Peake is sitting out, I'd say, probably in the back end of the first decade of the mine plan," he said. "There's real opportunities, particularly where current copper prices are, to bring that in a bit earlier."
